warnings: 79 of 324 elements have their recovery stations on the wrong side of the contour (centroid heuristic vs yaml e3; skin 7 of 230, web 72 of 94; sets {'layup_0': 7, 'layup_5': 72}): what the disagreement moves: the station positions (the y2, y3 columns of the .txt), the .vtk quads (the pictures), the displacement term z (omega x e3) of the u columns, the junction flags (computed from the positions) and the moment arms of the resultant integrals; NOT the stress and strain values, which the D route computes with the yaml's e3 and ply order (sg_dehom.py:56-61; measured on a NACA 0012 ring: ply stresses equal classical lamination theory with the yaml's outer-ply-first order to 3e-7, and dE11/dz of all 12 web elements follows the yaml e3)
frames: shell dialect: 324 per-element frames for 324 elements (e1 = beam axis on 324), used by the shell D route

units.note: OpenSG's (Pa) / (m) labels in the .txt are fixed text (cli.py:871-872)

sampling.layout: per ply (shell_recover.py: every ply sampled, ply and dz columns)
sampling.rule: stations per ply: m = the smallest odd number >= max(3, t_ply / (0.111111 h)), one station at the centre of each of m equal bands; every ply sampled (shell_recover.py)

coords: y2, y3 = yaml node columns 0, 1 (section axes); z = depth from the reference contour, zeta 0 = OML .. 1 = IML

ply_coverage.rule: stations per ply: m = the smallest odd number >= max(3, t_ply / (0.111111 h)), one station at the centre of each of m equal bands; every ply sampled (shell_recover.py)

per_ply.note: per set and ply (1 = the outer ply of the yaml layup): the largest |S_ij| over the stations in that ply, in the frame of the file, with (y2, y3, z)

law.order: [F1 F2 F3 M1 M2 M3] = C6 [eps11 gam12 gam13 kappa1 kappa2 kappa3]

applied_force.source: .ff key 1:/FF (VABS order F1 F2 F3 M1 M2 M3)

frame_rotation.to: wall axes (1 beam axis, 2 wall tangent, 3 inward normal)
frame_rotation.method: per station: S_wall = rotation_6x6(+angle) S_mat, E_wall = rotation_6x6(-angle)^T E_mat, angle = the yaml ply holding the station (the inverse of msg_rm_plate.py:632-634)
frame_rotation.weights: ply-share: the station's band dz (its share of its ply's thickness) x the element's arc length

wall_strains_fit.z: the .txt depth: 0 at the reference contour (OML, or the mid-surface at --center), positive along e3 (inward)
wall_strains_fit.feed: for 21 stations per ply, faces included, write the element's layup with opensg-homogenization's write_laminate_yaml.py (outer ply first = the bottom ply; --reference bottom for an OML run, mid for --center) and run `python -m opensg_solid.rm_plate_1D.cli_rm_plate dehom lam.yaml --strain e11 e22 g12 k11 k22 k12 2g13 2g23`; first check that its stresses at the station depths reproduce this element's shell stations (the skill has not validated this hand-over)

limitation: S13, S23 and S33 are not recovered by the first-order shell route (a model limit: the walls' through-thickness shear and normal stresses come back near zero; take them from a 2-D solid section or VABS where they matter)

mirrored_elements.affects: what the disagreement moves: the station positions (the y2, y3 columns of the .txt), the .vtk quads (the pictures), the displacement term z (omega x e3) of the u columns, the junction flags (computed from the positions) and the moment arms of the resultant integrals; NOT the stress and strain values, which the D route computes with the yaml's e3 and ply order (sg_dehom.py:56-61; measured on a NACA 0012 ring: ply stresses equal classical lamination theory with the yaml's outer-ply-first order to 3e-7, and dE11/dz of all 12 web elements follows the yaml e3)
mirrored_elements.finding: the D route places its depth stations along a centroid-heuristic normal (opensg_shell/cli.py:766-770: flip when (centroid - mid-arc) . n < 0, the centroid being the mean of the ring's nodes: it moves with the section, not with the origin; the API route keeps the same normal), not along the yaml's e3; on these elements the stations (and the .vtk quads) sit on the opposite side of the contour (outside the section at OML, in mirrored OML/IML order at center). Report it; never edit the engine

resultants.basis: ply-share: the station's band dz (its share of its ply's thickness) x the element's arc length weights; the wall shear pair rotated into section axes with each quad's tangent and normal; every element over its full length (409 duplicate jflag-3 stations kept: the shell model's own resultant), 0 NaN stations dropped
resultants.frame: wall axes, rotated back from the ply axes (frame_rotation)
resultants.formulas: F1 = int S11 dA, F2 = int s_1y2 dA, F3 = int s_1y3 dA, M1 = int (y2 s_1y3 - y3 s_1y2) dA, M2 = int y3 S11 dA, M3 = -int y2 S11 dA; s_1y2 = S12 t2 + S13 n2, s_1y3 = S12 t3 + S13 n3

gate.rule: every component: |recovered - applied| <= tolerance x max(|applied|, the cross term (F2/F3 share |F2|, |F3|; M2/M3 share |M2|, |M3|), the integral of its absolute density, 1e-4 x the load: the largest applied force or moment/r_max, r_max the largest station radius 7.201)
gate.statement: all six beam resultants are checked; the values are reported as integrated and never rescaled; S13, S23 and S33 are not recovered by the first-order shell route (a model limit: the walls' through-thickness shear and normal stresses come back near zero; take them from a 2-D solid section or VABS where they matter)

notes: the u1 u2 u3 columns are the RM warping at the element mid-arc + z (omega x e3), plus the .ff rigid motion u + y (C - I)^T (cli.py:846-861); compare differences, not values

material (ply-axis) table rotated back to the wall axes (1 beam axis, 2 wall tangent, 3 inward normal) station by station with its ply angle (0); the resultants and `stress_wall_axes` use it, the other statistics are ply axes
